scalars.scalar_value: Doctorate degree (Ph.D/Psy.D) in Clinical Psychology or related Psychology discipline

items.item_text: Doctorate degree (Ph.D/Psy.D) in Clinical Psychology or related Psychology discipline
Minimum 4-7 years of clinical experience
7+ years of clinical experience
Credentialing Requirement: A minimum of one year with current employer
Experience working in a university setting

DIRECT CLINICAL SERVICES: Applies advanced concepts to provide counseling, clinical consultation and/or psychotherapy to clients in a time-limited model. Develops and communicates treatment plans, utilizing acquired knowledge and appropriate therapeutic tools, including conducting psychological assessment as needed, and provides therapeutic crisis intervention/management as needed. Develops treatment plans in collaboration with the client; provides trauma informed, crisis intervention services and supports the management of critical mental health crises on campus as required. Utilizes acquired expertise and knowledge of the impact of intersectionality, multiculturalism, diversity, equity and inclusion on psychological service delivery in a university setting. (55% time)

OUTREACH AND EDUCATION SUPPORT: Provides outreach/ education, liaison services, committee representation and consultation services to UCR campus and community as a CAPS representative. Actively engages with supervisor and CAPS outreach coordinator in preparation, planning and participation in mental health related outreach programs, education and liaison work as well as in areas of specialty and in response to campus needs/requests. The percentage of time allocated to outreach activities may be adjusted throughout the year based on programmatic needs and outreach demand. In some cases, time allocated for outreach may be absorbed into direct service or other activity hours, depending on organizational priorities and workload distribution. (10% time)

SUPPORT AND EVALUATION FOR URGENT MENTAL HEALTH CONCERNS: Support and evaluation of student mental health. Provides urgent and crisis walk-in/virtual walk-in services supporting students and UC Riverside community in crisis intervention, consultation and triage. Support of campus crises/challenges, including crisis debrief/postvention services and other related crisis support services. Support and evaluation for students requiring mental health hospitalization and follow up. Occasional support for other UC campuses per reciprocity within system. (10% time)

APA ACCREDITED TRAINING PROGRAM PARTICIPATION: Actively participates in the UCR CAPS Pre-Doctoral Psychology Internship Program and in continuous professional development and training of interns. May include direct supervision of psychology interns’ clinical work, provision of didactic training, and service on training committee; support of intern psychological assessment activities; and general support of intern clinical needs. Will provide indirect support and supervision and mentorship to all interns. (10% time)

CLINICAL DOCUMENTAION, CASE MANAGEMENT AND RELATED BUSINESS PROCESSES: Completes accurate and concise clinical documentation for all clinical contacts in compliance with ethical and professional standards, adheres to UCR Quality Assurance policies, and in compliance with UCR CAPS policies and procedures. Manages caseload appropriately and with consultation as needed. (10% time)
Other duties as assigned by CAPS leadership (5% time)

Current, valid license to practice Psychology in California (or ability to gain licensure in CA prior to beginning work at UCR). Must maintain CA licensure through the Board of Psychology and maintain UCOP credentialing/privileging standards.
Read/Comprehend: Constantly
Write: Frequently
Perform Calculations: Occasionally
Communicate Orally: Constantly
Reason & Analyze: Constantly
Sit: Frequently
Stand: Occasionally
Walk: Occasionally

Thorough knowledge of working with diverse populations including but not limited to African American, Asian American, Latino/Latina, international, first-generation, veterans, students with disabilities, and LGBTQ. Understanding of intersectionality and how it impacts the daily lives of students.
Experience working with college students
Thorough skills associated with conducting complex diagnosis, problem-solving and critical-thinking
Demonstrated ability to effectively use interpersonal skills while representing the department on campus and to external units
Ability to conduct complex analysis and develop and present recommendations and course of treatment.
Highly effective written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.
Ability to work in a highly collaborative manner with diverse client group, members of the university staff and faculty.
Knowledge of electronic/medical records systems.
Demonstrated ability to perform trauma informed therapeutic services.
